newsitem.title: UK: Br Gas demerger - snapshot of Centrica.
newsitem.headline: Br Gas demerger - snapshot of Centrica.

text.p: British Gas Plc plans to split into two companies early next year. The following is a snapshot of Centrica, which will be floated off as a new listed company with its shares due to start trading on February 17.
Centrica will comprise the group's UK gas sales and trading activities and gas production from the Morecombe Bay gas fields, along with gas services and its chain of Energy Centre shops.
It will continue to use the British Gas brand, and the company said it will create a "major provider of gas and energy-related products and services to homes and business in Great Britain."
Led by Roy Gardner as chief executive, British Gas said it is anticipated that Centrica will be floated with no net debt.

It will have net assets of not less than 2.0 billion stg, after any further exceptional charges to be taken in the fourth quarter 1996 on take-or-pay gas purchase contracts and any provisions that may be made for deferred taxation.
Centrica does not anticipate paying dividends in the immediate future.
In the medium term, factors affecting possible dividends include the extent of competition into the domestic gas market and the extent to which Centrica can reduce gas purchase costs.
British Gas said Centrica will seek to reward shareholders through individual dividend payments or share repurchases depending on circumstances.
